subject: Post-demo: Eval harness onboarding + latency/streaming constraints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Eval harness onboarding + latency/streaming constraints

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the SLO/benchmark side.

Summary from our call
- Primary goal: validate that our inference stack can meet your interactive SLOs for the new clinician-facing summarization feature.
- Target KPIs you mentioned on the call: p95 latency under 250ms (endpoint-to-first-token) for 512-token summaries, sustained throughput to support ~120 concurrent users in peak, and streaming-first behavior (first tokens within 100ms when streaming enabled).
- Constraints: production traffic will come from Acme’s us-west region with on-prem EHR payloads, staging access is possible but behind a firewall.

What we’re sending now (attachments)
1) acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl — sanitized prompt set (5k samples, mixed dialog and clinical notes).
2) measurement-definitions-v1.md — definitions we propose for p50/p95/p99, cold-start vs warmed, and token-streaming latency.
3) redwood_eval_harness_v2.tar.gz (stub) — a packaged harness (README inside) that runs locally or in your staging environment; requires a whitelist/egress rule for the short-lived runner if you want Redwood to run it remotely.

Questions / asks for Acme
- Can you confirm the p95 target we should test to (250ms as noted) or adjust?
- Can you share a small staging endpoint we can hit (IP/CIDR) or confirm if you prefer us to run the harness inside your staging?
- Any additional prompt variants we should include (e.g., multi-turn context > 3 turns, or longer summaries up to 1k tokens)?

Proposed next steps
- You review attachments and confirm p95/p50 targets and whether we should run the harness from Redwood or you’d prefer internal execution. (Target: reply by Fri 3/6)
- If we run from Redwood: we’ll request a short-term IP whitelist and sign an access attestation.
- If Acme runs it: follow the README in redwood_eval_harness_v2 and return the harness outputs to the shared Drive link.

I’ll follow up with an internal TODO after we hear back.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (jsonl, ~5k lines, PII removed)
Attachment: measurement-definitions-v1.md (markdown, 3 pages)
Attachment: redwood_eval_harness_v2.tar.gz (archive, README included)
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Eval harness onboarding + latency/streaming constraints

Thanks, Jonas — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 250ms p95 is what clinical ops asked for as a goal, but engineering would accept an initial qualification at p95 < 350ms if we can see an improvement plan to 250ms within the same quarter. Can you include a suggested optimization path (batching, quantization profile, or smaller prompt variants) in your report?

- Streaming behavior is critical: our UI expects the first token to appear within ~80-120ms of request start for perceived responsiveness. Please measure both first-byte (time-to-first-token) and per-chunk latency for streaming (we typically use 50-token chunks).

- Regarding execution: we prefer Redwood run the harness first against a staging endpoint we provide (easier for us to validate). We will open a temporary inbound rule for your runner — let me know the egress IPs.

- Prompt variants: please include 3-turn and 5-turn context variants plus one long-note summarization (800–1,000 tokens).

I’ll loop in our infra owner for the whitelist once you send the runner IPs and attestation.

—Sarah
Sarah Li
Product Lead, Clinical AI | Acme Health
sarah.li@acmehealth.com

On Wed, Mar 4, 2026 at 3:08 PM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the SLO/benchmark side.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Eval harness onboarding + latency/streaming constraints

Thanks Sarah — great, we can accommodate that approach. Quick responses inline and a couple of requests: 

- p95 target: we’ll run the first pass against p95 < 350ms as you requested, then provide an improvement plan to reach 250ms (typical levers: model variant selection, int8 quantization, prefix/KV caching for warmed flows). We’ll document expected unit-cost delta per lever.

- Streaming metrics: we’ll add measurements for time-to-first-token and per-50-token chunk latencies. Our harness supports measuring token-emission times at 10ms resolution.

- Runner IPs: Redwood will run the harness from an ephemeral runner. Attestation and exact egress IPs are attached in measurement-definitions-v1.md (section 4) — if you need CIDR format we can provide that.

- Prompt variants: included and attached in acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (3-turn, 5-turn, and long-note sets).

Permission request to run: Can Acme provision a temporary staging endpoint and add these egress IP(s): 34.201.33.12, 34.201.33.13 (these are Redwood ephemeral runners). We’ll only run against the staging endpoint and will share logs and raw harness output in the Drive link.

Timing: if we get the whitelist by Mon 3/9 we can run the first pass and share a summary by Thu 3/12. Does that timeline work?

If ok, we’ll also add Marissa + Aditya to the Slack thread for technical handoff during the run.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: measurement-definitions-v1.md (contains runner IPs and attestation template)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 6 Mar 2026 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Eval harness onboarding + latency/streaming constraints — internal action items

Internal team — forwarding Acme thread and Sarah's confirmations. Action items and notes:

1) Consent and runner prep (Marissa)
- Prepare ephemeral runner image with redwood_eval_harness_v2 and the measurement flags we discussed: --measure-t2ft --chunk-size 50 --deterministic-seed 0 --sample-temperature 0.0
- Validate harness writes: per-request token timestamps, p50/p95/p99, cold start separation, and per-chunk latency CSV.

2) Measurement definitions (Aditya)
- Finalize measurement-definitions-v1.md: ensure we define endpoint-to-first-token (E2FT), server-first-byte vs token-emission, and the methodology for warm vs cold runs (5 warmups, 100 measured iterations).

3) Access/ops (Soojin)
- Coordinate whitelist request: target egress IPs 34.201.33.12/32 and 34.201.33.13/32. Attach attestation template to the Drive.

4) Customer comms (Jonas)
- Confirm timeline: ask Acme to provide the staging endpoint and whitelist by Mon 3/9 so we can deliver a first-run summary by Thu 3/12.

Notes: Sarah accepted an initial qualification at p95 < 350ms with a roadmap to 250ms. Streaming first-token target: 80–120ms. Include per-chunk (50-token) latency and cost delta estimates for each optimization.

Please ack and add estimated ETA for your tasks. I’ll create a Slack channel once we have whitelist confirmation.

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
